expectations.text: Rejects the "below 40% lurkers" target and states that around 90% of members never posting is the baseline condition, not a launch defect
expectations.evidence: '"Get non-posters below 40%" is the wrong target — don't ship it.' ... 'roughly 90% of members never post, 9% post occasionally, 1% account for most activity. Lurking is the baseline condition of every online community, not a defect to fix.'

expectations.text: Attributes the 90-9-1 participation-inequality finding to Jakob Nielsen at NN/g rather than presenting it as an unsourced rule of thumb
expectations.evidence: "Jakob Nielsen's 90-9-1 rule (NN/g, 2006, the most-replicated finding in community measurement)" with source link to nngroup.com/articles/participation-inequality/

expectations.text: Notes that the beta group's four-in-five read-only share is at or better than that baseline rather than a problem to fix
expectations.evidence: "Read against that baseline, the beta's 'four in five just read' (80% lurk) is already better than typical — most communities never get below 90%."

expectations.text: Rejects the 2,000-member target as a joins counter rather than a health signal
expectations.evidence: Table row: "2,000 members by day 90 | Keep, but report as context only | Member count is a joins counter, not a health signal — a well-marketed room can hit 2,000 with 20 weekly posters and still be a failed launch"

expectations.text: Sets targets on the number of active members and on ratio signals instead
expectations.evidence: "Replacement: target the count and rate of active members directly, not the inverse of the lurker share." and "≥ 20% of members active in the trailing 30 days (≈400 people at 2,000 members), reported as an absolute count alongside the ratio"

expectations.text: Proposes day-90 pass thresholds covering at least: answered within 24 hours, non-staff share of posts, new members posting within 7 days, monthly active share, threads with at least one reply, and top-five engagement concentration
expectations.evidence: Table in §3 lists all six: "Questions answered within 24h", "Posts written by non-staff", "New members posting within 7 days", "Monthly active / total members", "Threads with ≥ 1 reply", "Engagement share of top 5 members"

expectations.text: Labels which thresholds are published findings and which are baselines offered as a starting hypothesis to recalibrate
expectations.evidence: "Metric definitions are published practice; cutoff values are practitioner baselines to recalibrate once Palebright has its own trailing data — treat them as a starting hypothesis, not a standard." with each table row's Basis column marked "Baseline practice"

expectations.text: Requires the thresholds be written down before launch rather than assessed afterwards, and says why
expectations.evidence: "## 6. Fold-back criteria (set now, not at day 90)" and "Decision owner: name this person now. Whoever owns the day-90 read should also be the one authorized to pull the trigger — otherwise the fold-back becomes a debate instead of a decision." plus §4's rationale: "A single day-90 check means the first time anyone looks, it's too late in the quarter to fix anything cheaply."

expectations.text: Recommends publishing a response-time commitment and places it inside a 48-hour window
expectations.evidence: The transcript cites 48h evidence only as rationale ("contributors who got a response within 48h returned and contributed again at a much higher rate") and sets an internal metric of 24h ("Questions answered within 24h") plus a day-30 checkpoint of "under a few hours" — no explicit recommendation to publish a public response-time commitment/SLA set at 48 hours.

expectations.text: Cites the 48-hour responsiveness evidence as a published finding rather than an invented target
expectations.evidence: "Source for the day-30 rule and the 48h-response evidence: Mozilla study cited in GitHub's Open Source Guides — contributors who got a response within 48h returned and contributed again at a much higher rate... [opensource.guide/building-community]"
